headline: CHINA ENDS RETAIL PAPER GOLD TRADING — ICBC AND FOUR MAJOR BANKS EXIT SGE MARKET EFFECTIVE JULY 24
snippet: China's five largest retail banks — ICBC, China Construction Bank, Postal Savings Bank of China, Ping An Bank, and China Guangfa Bank — terminated individual leveraged paper gold trading products linked to the Shanghai Gold Exchange effective July 24, 2026, the deadline set when ICBC issued its wind-down notice on June 24. The policy targets speculative retail positions only; physical gold purchases, gold ETFs, and the SGE's institutional markets are entirely unaffected. Retail clients had three choices before the deadline: close positions, liquidate holdings, or take physical delivery. Market analysts interpret the move as Beijing accelerating a structural shift toward physical price discovery at a time when gold sits at roughly $4,055/oz — down about 28% from January's record near $5,600. Removing a large paper-supply-generating mechanism may tighten the bid-ask between spot and forward markets, forcing retail Chinese demand through bullion, coins, and ETF channels that directly support physical prices rather than synthetic exposure — a structural positive for junior gold producers pricing their reserves at spot.

headline: GOLD DEFENDS $4,050, SILVER REBOUNDS 2% AS IRAN OIL TOPS $100 AND FED BLACKOUT BEGINS — JULY 29 RATE DECISION NOW 34% HIKE
snippet: Gold spot opened July 24 at $4,053.40/oz and held near $4,055–4,057 as the Federal Reserve entered its pre-meeting blackout period ahead of the July 28-29 FOMC decision. Silver recovered from Thursday's selling to $58.40/oz, up 1.98% on the day, as physical buyers stepped into the pullback. The macro driver: Brent crude crossed $100/barrel for the first time since May after the U.S. conducted additional airstrikes on Iran and Houthi forces targeted two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, raising chokepoint-disruption risk on global supply. Surging energy prices have pushed markets to price a 34% probability of a July 29 rate hike — up sharply from single digits two weeks ago — and more than 81% odds of a September increase. Jobless claims printed 187,000, far below the 212,000 forecast, reinforcing the Fed's tightening case. Year-end consensus from J.P. Morgan and HSBC still places gold at $4,750–$6,300, suggesting the current level is deeply discounted to institutional targets if the Fed signals a true hold path at next week's meeting.

headline: SOMA GOLD AURORA MINE GETS TRIPLE PRODUCTION PERMIT IN COLOMBIA — 75 TPD CLEARED AT 4.5 g/t Au; RAMP BEGINS (TSXV: SOMA)
snippet: Colombia's Agencia Nacional de Minería granted Soma Gold Corp. (TSXV: SOMA) a new Permiso de Trabajo de Obra on July 17, 2026, authorizing Aurora Mine throughput to triple from 25 tonnes per day to 75 TPD — with the permit effective immediately. Soma announced the authorization on July 24. Near-term production is expected to ramp to 30–40 TPD at an average grade of approximately 4.5 g/t gold before scaling toward the full 75 TPD limit as mining logistics are optimized. Soma operates three producing Colombian gold assets; the expanded Aurora permit de-risks a key bottleneck in its growth plan without requiring additional capital expenditure. At 4.5 g/t gold and 75 TPD, the theoretical full-rate production profile substantially upgrades Soma's free-cash-flow potential for H2 2026, and with gold above $4,050/oz the incremental margin on each additional tonne processed is significant for a company at this market-cap scale.

headline: TOCVAN HITS 581 g/t SILVER AT SURFACE AT GRAN PILAR — NEW ZONE 900M FROM PILOT FACILITY; FIRST DORÉ POUR Q4 2026 (CSE: TOC)
snippet: Tocvan Ventures Corp. (CSE: TOC) announced July 23 the discovery of a new at-surface mineralized silver-gold zone located 900 metres east of its fully permitted 50,000-tonne Gran Pilar heap-leach pilot facility in Sonora, Mexico. Hole JES-26-152 returned 1.5 metres grading 2.2 g/t Au and 581 g/t Ag within a broader vein corridor — confirming a robust new target directly adjacent to planned infrastructure, a geometry that could feed the pilot operation without additional trucking costs. The Gran Pilar pilot facility is construction-ready and targeting its first gold-silver doré pour in Q4 2026, with 70% gold recovery modeled over 60–90 day leach cycles at 50,000 tonnes per phase. The discovery extends the project's resource growth potential simultaneously with the transition toward cash-flow generation — an optionality combination that rarely appears at the CSE junior level.

headline: SCOTTIE RESOURCES: 10,000M DOWN, 7 RIGS ACTIVE IN BC GOLDEN TRIANGLE — FEASIBILITY STUDY ON TRACK FOR H1 2027 (TSXV: SCOT)
snippet: Scottie Resources Corp. (TSXV: SCOT) reported July 23 that it has completed more than 10,000 metres across 47 holes in its fully financed 50,000-metre drill program at the Scottie Gold Mine Project — 35 kilometres north of Stewart, British Columbia in the Golden Triangle. Seven diamond drill rigs are running simultaneously, targeting the Blueberry Contact Zone, Scottie Gold Mine vein, Bend Vein, C and D Zones, Serac Vein, Lakebed, and the Domino target — a multi-zone simultaneous strategy that accelerates data generation for the combined Feasibility Study and updated Mineral Resource Estimate targeted for H1 2027. The 50,000-metre program is Scottie's largest ever and was designed at a gold price that now looks conservative: every dollar increase above $4,000/oz adds meaningfully to the project's projected economics at a district known for some of BC's highest historic underground gold grades.

headline: ACHILLES GOES DEEP: AGC DRILLS 26m AT 102 g/t AgEq FROM 433m — MINERAL SYSTEM CONFIRMED OPEN 540m BELOW SURFACE (ASX: AGC)
source_name: Discovery Alert / Australian Gold and Copper
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper Ltd. (ASX: AGC) reported that its deepest Achilles drill hole to date — A3DD014 — returned 26 metres at 102 g/t silver equivalent from 433 metres depth, including a 15-metre interval at 153 g/t AgEq and a 2-metre ultra-high-grade intercept at 770 g/t AgEq. The result extends known mineralisation approximately 290 metres below the base of the December 2025 Mineral Resource Estimate, confirming the Achilles polymetallic system to at least 540 metres down dip from surface. Managing Director Glen Diemar stated the system is 'open and fertile hundreds of metres below the current resource.' The current MRE was modeled on surface-to-250m geometry; the depth extension now provides geological support for an underground mining assessment and a resource expansion — a significant re-rating catalyst for an ASX junior previously evaluated primarily as an open-pit target.

headline: DISTRICT METALS VIKEN PEA: US$2.88B NPV, NEGATIVE-COST URANIUM AS SWEDEN ENDS 40-YEAR BAN (TSXV: DMX)
snippet: District Metals Corp. (TSXV: DMX) filed its NI 43-101 PEA Technical Report on July 20, 2026 — five days after Sweden's new legislation facilitating uranium mining came into force on July 15 — for the Viken Energy Metals Deposit, the largest undeveloped uranium resource in the world. The PEA outlines an after-tax NPV8% of US$2.88 billion, IRR of 45.9%, and payback period of 2.1 years for a conventional open-pit operation producing an average 3.3 million lbs U3O8 per year over a 13-year mine life. After vanadium, potash, and other by-product credits, the net operating cost of uranium calculates to negative US$121/lb U3O8 — meaning by-products alone more than offset the cost of uranium production. Viken carries the largest undeveloped uranium Mineral Resource globally alongside significant vanadium, potash, molybdenum, nickel, copper, and zinc — a multi-commodity critical minerals play now actionable under Swedish law for the first time in four decades.

headline: COPPER FOX SOMBRERO BUTTE: UPDATED MODEL DEFINES LARGE PORPHYRY Cu-Mo TARGET IN ARIZONA LARAMIDE BELT (TSXV: CUU)
snippet: Copper Fox Metals Inc. (TSXV: CUU) released July 24 an updated exploration model for its 100%-owned Sombrero Butte project in Pinal County, Arizona — integrating geophysics, alteration, mineralogy, fluid inclusion studies, and historical drilling to define a large near-surface porphyry copper-molybdenum target within the Laramide copper province. The updated model supports interpretation of a large, highly evolved porphyry Cu-Mo system in the same geological belt that hosts Resolution, Superior, and Ray — some of the largest copper mines in North America. The near-surface target geometry improves economics relative to deeper porphyry systems; Arizona's established Laramide Cu-Mo permitting framework is among the most predictable in the western United States. Copper Fox is advancing permitting plans to enable drill testing of the defined target as copper approaches a new U.S. COMEX record.

headline: 3 URANIUM STOCKS TO OWN BEFORE JULY ENDS — LONG-TERM CONTRACTS AT 18-YEAR HIGHS AS NUCLEAR DEMAND OUTPACES EQUITIES
snippet: With the long-term uranium contract price reaching $94/lb — an 18-year high — while uranium mining equities badly lagged the metal in H1 (junior miners down 7.4%; major indexes down 14–17% in June alone), 247 Wall Street's July 23 analysis argues the risk-off selloff has created a compelling setup. The three picks are Cameco (NYSE: CCJ), back at full Cigar Lake capacity following its brief July shutdown; Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU), on pace to hit full-year uranium production guidance by mid-year with multi-commodity critical minerals production in uranium, rare earths, and vanadium; and NexGen Energy (NYSE: NXE), whose Arrow deposit in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin represents one of the highest-grade undeveloped uranium projects globally with a construction permit expected before year-end. A Section 232 decision on uranium trade policy expected before month-end could impose domestic-sourcing rules that would immediately tighten the already-undersupplied U.S. enrichment pipeline and act as a direct catalyst for all three names.

headline: MONEY METALS: GOLD-SILVER RATIO AT 70:1 IS A BUYING SIGNAL — SILVER HISTORICALLY OUTPERFORMS FROM THIS EXTREME
snippet: Money Metals Exchange published July 23 analysis arguing that the gold-silver ratio expanding from near 55:1 in May to approximately 70:1 by mid-July — its highest in more than a year — is a contrarian setup for silver rather than a warning to avoid the metal. The 50-year modern historical average sits between 60:1 and 70:1, placing silver at the upper edge of its long-term relative cheapness versus gold at current levels. Silver has fallen more than 52% from its January 2026 all-time high of $121.62 to approximately $58/oz, while gold has held better, declining roughly 28% from its $5,600 record. Institutional forecasters have not revised their targets — JPMorgan's silver base case remains $81/oz and the LBMA 2026 consensus sits at $79.57/oz — suggesting the ratio widening reflects near-term risk-off flows rather than a structural demand shift. The Silver Institute confirmed a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit in 2026 at 46.3 million ounces, up 15% from 2025, which provides a fundamental underpinning that ratio extremes historically reward patient buyers.
